chapter: Biddle, Durham and early road shows
title: Drugstore band in Helena with Joseph Patterson and the Syncopated Six
summary: He played in the back of a crowded Helena drugstore, brought in guitarist Joseph Patterson, and the owner added the Syncopated Six, including Floyd Campbell and Cranston Hamilton.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: To Arkansas, Helena, Arkansas. And I played in a drug store. Believe it or not -- piano, drums and trumpet -- we played in the back of the drug store. They were selling roast beef sandwiches and brown gravy and so forth and I'm telling you that place was just like that.

Crowded. Well, I told the man, I says, "I have a very fine guitarist I know of back in Durham, North Carolina. I'd like to add him in the band here." So, the man told me to send and get him. So, I sent and got him and his name was Joseph Patterson. You'll read about that though, in that book about Patterson. So, I had Patterson, and I sent for Patterson and that's where we played. (unintelligible) Then we were trying -- and there was another place -- that man was about to go out of business, so he sent and got Swayzee and the rest of those boys, called themselves the Syncopated Six. I think they had played with Mamie Smith's Jazz Hounds.
Swese, yes, I know that name.
Yes. Swayzee trumpeter, [popular band.] Pretty good trumpeter.
This was in Helena -- Helena, Arkansas. So, we had banjo, trumpet, drums -- Floyd Campbell on drums --
Yes, uh-huh. Floyd Campbell did, had a band here and played here for quite a while. Yeah. And Cranston Hamilton -- he's dead now, he died not too long ago.

He played piano. Oh, (unintelligible) and he really played but didn't read a lick. He didn't read nothing, just played. He played something, he really played. He played with Charlie Creath and everything. So, --
